scenes.visual: Title card 'Leaks That Multiply' over a hillside: PINK monkeyflowers near the top, RED monkeyflowers near the bottom. COLOUR MAP (shared by both films, the take-homes and the lesson): M. lewisii always PINK flowers with a fuzzy BUMBLEBEE; M. cardinalis always RED tubular flowers with a HUMMINGBIRD; gene flow = a stream of small GOLD dots; each barrier = a GREY gate with its strength printed on it; a vertical DASHED line labelled 'zygote' sits right after the fertilization gate and separates prezygotic gates (left) from postzygotic gates (right); benthic stickleback OLIVE and deep-bodied, limnetic stickleback SILVER-BLUE and slender. All numbers appear only as on-screen text. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: These two monkeyflowers can be crossed by hand, and the cross makes hybrid seed. So why do almost no genes pass between them in the wild?
scenes.visual: A paintbrush carries pollen from a PINK flower to a RED flower; a seed labelled 'hybrid seed' drops. Cut to the wild hillside: GOLD dots try to drift from the pink plants to the red plants and almost all fade out. Big question mark.
scenes.narration: These two monkeyflowers can be crossed by hand, and the cross makes hybrid seed. So why do almost no genes pass between them in the wild?

scenes.tts: Gene flow is the movement of genes between populations through mating. Picture it as a stream. Each gold dot is one chance for genes to cross to the other species.
scenes.visual: A counter reading '1,000' appears beside a stream of GOLD dots leaving the PINK plants and flowing right, toward the RED plants. Label 'gene flow (schematic)'. Small note: 'each dot = a potential path for genes: carried by pollen before the zygote, by a hybrid and its gametes after it'.
scenes.narration: Gene flow is the movement of genes between populations through mating. Picture it as a stream. Each gold dot is one chance for genes to cross to the other species.

scenes.tts: A reproductive barrier is anything that reduces gene flow between populations. You might expect one wall that stops everything. These monkeyflowers have no such wall. Each of their barriers is partial.
scenes.visual: A single tall black wall slides into the stream labelled 'one complete wall?'; it is crossed out with a red X and dissolves. In its place a row of GREY gates appears, each with gaps that let some GOLD dots through.
scenes.narration: A reproductive barrier is anything that reduces gene flow between populations. You might expect one wall that stops everything. These monkeyflowers have no such wall. Each of their barriers is partial.

scenes.tts: So picture the barriers as gates, in the order life meets them. First, where the plants grow. Then, which pollinator visits. Then, whether the other species' pollen can fertilize the egg.
scenes.visual: Gates labelled in turn as the narrator names them: 'habitat (ecogeographic)', 'pollinator' (with a bumblebee on the pink side, a hummingbird on the red side), 'pollen and fertilization'. The GOLD stream flows left to right toward them.
scenes.narration: So picture the barriers as gates, in the order life meets them. First, where the plants grow. Then, which pollinator visits. Then, whether the other species' pollen can fertilize the egg.

scenes.tts: Fertilization makes the zygote, the fertilized egg. Gates before it are prezygotic. Gates after it, such as hybrids that fail to survive or are sterile, are postzygotic.
scenes.visual: A vertical DASHED line labelled 'zygote' drops into place immediately after the 'pollen and fertilization' gate. Bracket on the left: 'prezygotic'. Two more gates appear on the right: 'hybrid seed and survival', 'hybrid fertility'. Bracket on the right: 'postzygotic'.
scenes.narration: Fertilization makes the zygote, the fertilized egg. Gates before it are prezygotic. Gates after it, such as hybrids that fail to survive or are sterile, are postzygotic.

scenes.tts: Here is the key. When gates act one after another, each acts only on what earlier gates let through. A pollinator cannot carry pollen between plants that never grow near each other.
scenes.visual: Highlight the pollinator gate: only the GOLD dots that got past the habitat gate reach it; dots stopped at the habitat gate turn grey and stay behind. A bumblebee hovers over pink flowers far up the slope, red flowers far below, no path between them.
scenes.narration: Here is the key. When gates act one after another, each acts only on what earlier gates let through. A pollinator cannot carry pollen between plants that never grow near each other.

scenes.tts: Try three partial gates, each stopping seventy percent of the dots that reach it. Together, do they stop seventy percent? More than a hundred? Something else?
scenes.visual: Clean diagram: three identical GREY gates each marked '70%'. Counter '1,000' at the start. Three answer cards float above: '70%?', '210%?', 'something else?'.
scenes.narration: Try three partial gates, each stopping seventy percent of the dots that reach it. Together, do they stop seventy percent? More than a hundred? Something else?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The three answer cards hold; a 5-second ring timer counts down in the corner.

scenes.tts: Watch the counter. Each gate leaves less for the next one. In the end, about ninety-seven dots in every hundred are stopped. That stops more than any single gate, yet a few dots still pass all three.
scenes.visual: Dots stream through: counter drops 1,000 → 300 → 90 → 27 as each gate is passed. Final card: 'stopped: 97.3%'. The '70%?' and '210%?' cards fade; '210%' gets the note 'impossible: more than all the gene flow'. Computed, not schematic.
scenes.narration: Watch the counter. Each gate leaves less for the next one. In the end, about ninety-seven dots in every hundred are stopped. That stops more than any single gate, yet a few dots still pass all three.

scenes.tts: That is the rule. The fractions that get through multiply. Several leaky gates in a row can block nearly all gene flow. Adding their strengths is wrong, because the sum can pass one hundred percent.
scenes.visual: On-screen line builds: 'left = 0.3 × 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.027'. Below it, a crossed-out line '70% + 70% + 70% = 210%'. Then a general line: 'gene flow left = (1 − RI1) × (1 − RI2) × (1 − RI3)', with 'RI = share of the remaining gene flow a barrier stops'.
scenes.narration: That is the rule. The fractions that get through multiply. Several leaky gates in a row can block nearly all gene flow. Adding their strengths is wrong, because the sum can pass one hundred percent.

scenes.tts: Now the real monkeyflowers. Ramsey, Bradshaw and Schemske measured these gates one stage at a time. They worked in the field and in the greenhouse. Every gate was partial.
scenes.visual: Back to the hillside with PINK and RED plants. Caption 'Ramsey, Bradshaw & Schemske, 2003'. A clipboard labelled 'measured components summarized' ticks broad groups in turn: 'range overlap', 'pollinator isolation', 'pollen precedence' (all left of the DASHED zygote line), then 'F1 fitness: germination, survival, flowering, growth and fertility' (right of the line). No per-group values are shown. Each gate shows gaps.
scenes.narration: Now the real monkeyflowers. Ramsey, Bradshaw and Schemske measured these gates one stage at a time. They worked in the field and in the greenhouse. Every gate was partial.

scenes.tts: Where the plants grow, and which pollinator visits, came first in the sequence. Most of the stream was gone before any hybrid could form.
scenes.visual: The GOLD stream thins sharply at the habitat and pollinator gates; only a trickle reaches the DASHED zygote line. Label on the trickle: 'most isolation before any hybrid forms'. Dot counts here are schematic (labelled 'schematic').
scenes.narration: Where the plants grow, and which pollinator visits, came first in the sequence. Most of the stream was gone before any hybrid could form.

scenes.tts: Together, the measured barriers were estimated to block, on average, almost all gene flow. No one gate could explain that alone.
scenes.caption: Together, the measured barriers were estimated to block, on average, almost all gene flow. No one gate could explain that alone.
scenes.visual: A total card appears: 'measured barriers together: 99.87% of gene flow blocked (estimate; mean of the two directions)'. All gates glow together; the stream past the last gate is a few faint dots.
scenes.narration: Together, the measured barriers were estimated to block, on average, almost all gene flow. No one gate could explain that alone.

scenes.tts: This is also why a species pair does not need sterile hybrids. When the early gates are strong, few hybrids form at all.
scenes.visual: The postzygotic gates on the right dim and turn transparent, labelled 'what if hybrids were fertile?'; the stream reaching them is still only a trickle, so little changes. Label: 'few hybrids form'.
scenes.narration: This is also why a species pair does not need sterile hybrids. When the early gates are strong, few hybrids form at all.

scenes.tts: So two species need no perfect wall. Several leaky gates, acting one after another, can cut the gene flow between them to a trickle.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full row of GREY gates with the GOLD stream thinning to a few faint dots at the right (never to nothing). PINK flowers with the bumblebee on the left, RED flowers with the hummingbird on the right, apart.
scenes.narration: So two species need no perfect wall. Several leaky gates, acting one after another, can cut the gene flow between them to a trickle.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex, the hexagon mascot, holding a tiny grey gate. Line: 'Each barrier blocks only what earlier barriers let through, so leaks multiply.'
